checks: Relative affine dimension is the base projection rank plus d because there is a positive d-dimensional fiber. An active nonvertical facet must exist at every regular fiber boundary point, since pure-base inequalities do not constrain the continuous fiber.

An active nonzero continuous facet normal supports the actual fiber and is its unique normalized normal at a regular point. The finite first-facet choice is Borel. For each chosen facet the nonnegative affine gap has conditional mean zero, so the target row stays in that facet.

The second marginal is the marked surface measure, hence it gives no mass to the irregular set or the finitely many exceptional agreement sets. The first marginal is absolutely continuous with respect to the same measure, so the source agreement also holds. This does not discard seams merely because they are ambient-null.

For an active affine piece, its conditional expectation equals its source value. Subtracting the concave value leaves a nonnegative gap, and a zero expectation is equivalent to support on the closed equality set. This applies to every active piece, including ties. Source 332fa99ca9bb69c2 §1 (1) and §4 (6) have the same scope.

overlap.comparison: The marked physical coupling preserves fiber normals and anchored support equality. It does not state the Jensen test for independently specified concave functions on ambient facets or the affine-piece equality criterion.
This computes an actual particular visible-star surface density and its representative seams. The draft establishes a general test for any function with the stated facet agreement.

readability: The statement and proof specify the necessary hypotheses and quantities.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The physical martingale keeps each row in a genuine containing facet. Conditional Jensen applies to that facet's own concave function, including regular seams of positive fiber surface measure, and the finite affine-piece equality condition is exact.
